basis: The defining triad comprises deafness, small-bowel diverticula and neuropathy; no additional organ involvement established.
Glioblastoma arising in the brain stem.
Breast-associated symptom syndrome without established damage to a covered organ; symptoms do not establish neurologic, muscle or autoimmune disease.
Developmental speech-fluency disorder classified as a neurological communication disorder.
Thrombosis of intracranial venous sinuses; headache reflects pressure, while lasting brain injury is not established in at least 30%.
Congenital supernumerary digits define this skeletal disorder; additional organs vary across syndromic subtypes.
Carcinoma involving lymph-node tissue, which has no specified axis; neither lymphoma nor blood-cell malignancy, and a covered primary origin is unspecified.
Acquired lanugo hair disorder; glossitis and tongue enlargement occur in 30-79%. Associated cancers are separate diseases; eyelid morphology alone lacks damage.
Meningoceles with skeletal/connective-tissue abnormalities; hearing impairment 80-99%, ptosis 6/6. Sleep apnea 3/4 and keloids 4/6 omitted under the four-axis cap.
Direct traumatic injury to peripheral nerves.
Neonatal thyroid hormone excess, predominantly mediated by transplacental thyroid-stimulating antibodies; tachycardia alone is not cardiac damage.
Inherited intrahepatic bile-handling disorder; proteinuria in 3/3 supports renal involvement. Prolonged PTT alone does not establish direct blood-system disease.
Dentine dysplasia affects teeth; generalized long-bone osteosclerosis is also defining. Narrow marrow spaces alone do not establish blood-cell dysfunction.
Embryopathy defined by microcephaly, intellectual disability and cardiac malformations; affected offspring do not themselves have phenylketonuria.
Tessier 5 cleft traverses the upper lip, maxillary skeleton and lateral lower eyelid/orbital rim; these are defining anatomical defects.
Focal neurological movement disorder; involuntary muscle contractions do not establish primary skeletal-muscle damage.
Serine-biosynthesis defect with defining neurodevelopmental injury and seizures; esotropia occurs in 30-79%. Cataract, anemia and ichthyosis are each below 30%.
Platelet deficiency with purpura; this broad category does not specify an immune mechanism. Purpura alone does not establish lasting skin damage.
Defining features include craniosynostosis, contractures and scoliosis, together with cleft palate and ear malformation.
Direct chemical injury and inflammation of the colon; chemical inflammation does not establish infection or an immune-mediated mechanism.
Hereditary blood/marrow neoplastic syndrome. Possible lymphoma, autoimmune disease and skin findings do not establish common additional involvement.
Defining intellectual and developmental impairment; recurrent infections 4/4 do not establish intrinsic immunodeficiency. Minor digital and joint traits lack established dysfunction.
GM2 storage causes severe neurodegeneration and common progressive retinal/visual dysfunction (>30%); ocular label is not based on the cherry-red spot alone. Hepatosplenomegaly <30%.
Carcinoma arising in the urinary bladder; neuroendocrine histology does not establish endocrine-gland disease. Hypercalcemia occurs in fewer than 30%.
Congenital split spinal cord; associated vertebral malformations and scoliosis affect roughly half or more and represent structural skeletal involvement.
